My land has always been wheat and corn. My father grew wheat and corn on this same ground, and his father before him. I have 5 mu here in Quzhou. The soil is decent loam, the water table is still reachable with our pump, and the county seed station has the inputs I need. I am not going to gamble on cotton or vegetables — I don't have the connections to get good prices, and I'm not young enough to take that kind of risk.

This year will be the same rotation I've done every year. I already planted the winter wheat back in October — that crop is already in the ground and coming along fine. Now I'm thinking ahead to the summer. Once I harvest the wheat in June, I'll turn around immediately and plant corn on the same 5 mu. No point letting the land sit idle.

For the wheat: I used Jimai-22 seed from the county station. It's an improved variety, good resistance to lodging. I applied base fertilizer at planting — diammonium phosphate mostly. I'll topdress urea at jointing. I irrigate four times — pre-winter, jointing, heading, and grain filling. Water is expensive but wheat won't do without it here. I'll spray fungicide for rust twice and once more for aphids near heading. I rotary-tilled before sowing.

For the corn: I'll plant directly into the wheat stubble with the no-till seeder the village cooperative has. Zhengdan-958 hybrid seed — reliable, everyone uses it, and I know what to expect. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting and chase it with urea at the big-bell stage. Summer rains usually handle most of the water, but I'll pump once if August turns dry. One herbicide spray after emergence, that's enough.

I expect around 450 kg/mu from the wheat and maybe 550 from the corn. Nothing fancy. Stable income. That's what matters at my age.
